gaps.sentence: He ___ some ridiculous excuse about his car breaking down.
gaps.explanation: make an excuse is the fixed collocation; 'tell an excuse' is not used.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: It was the manager's job to ___ the bad news to the staff.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the news to somebody
gaps.explanation: break the news to somebody means to tell them something difficult or upsetting first.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her a compliment on her new hairstyle.
gaps.explanation: pay somebody a compliment is the fixed collocation for praising someone.

gaps.sentence: It took her years to ___ a living from her painting.
gaps.explanation: make a living means to earn enough money to live on.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ losses of two million last year.
He ___ a fortune by buying his train ticket in advance.
gaps.explanation: save a fortune means to avoid spending a large amount; buying in advance keeps money.

gaps.sentence: Local residents are deeply ___ about the new motorway plan.
gaps.explanation: deeply concerned is the standard collocation meaning very worried; the other adjectives do not collocate with 'deeply'.
